name: data-table
purpose: The data-driven table: pass `data` + `columns` and it renders the header, rows, selection, sorting, empty / loading / error states itself, through the same `Table` parts (`Table.Header`, `Table.Row`, `Table.HeadCell`, `Table.Cell`), so its markup, tokens and accessibility are those of [`table`](table.md). The headless **`@tanstack/vue-table`** engine lives here and only here: a hand-composed `Table` never loads it. A top **toolbar band** (`title` / `toolbar` / `filters` slots) sits above the scroll viewport for a title, the context-aware `Table.*` toolbar parts (search, filter, export, refresh, live) and removable filter chips; the `toolbar` and `filters` slots are scoped with the TanStack `table` instance so the consumer can drive filtering, global search and column visibility through the table's own methods. Optional features are **companion parts** that read the table's context (`compound-api.md`, CODE_QUALITY 3.4): `DataTablePagination` in the `footer` slot pages the rows with [`Pagination`](pagination.md), `DataTableLoadMore` in the `load-more` slot asks for the next rows, and the toolbar parts own the search text, the structured filters, the live tail and the export rows. A root-only table loads none of them. **Engine.** DataTable is driven by **`@tanstack/vue-table`** (`useVueTable` + `getCoreRowModel` / `getSortedRowModel` / `getFilteredRowModel` / `getPaginationRowModel`), covering sorting, pagination, row selection, column visibility, and global filtering — client- and server-side (`manualSorting` / `manualFiltering` on the root, `manual` on `DataTablePagination`). It is a pure-logic library (no markup/styles/positioning/animation), granted narrowly to the table family (this component and the editable `data-grid` that builds on it) per [`.claude/rules/dependencies.md`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/.claude/rules/dependencies.md) § Exceptions; rendering stays 100% in our primitives. State is exposed via v-model in webkit shapes: `sorting`, `selectedKeys`, `columnVisibility` and `openKeys` on the root, `page` + `pageSize` on `DataTablePagination`, the search text on `TableSearch`, the structured filters on `TableFilter` and the live tail on `TableLiveButton`; the component adapts them to the engine internally, and `getSnapshot()` / `setSnapshot()` read and write all of them at once. `@tanstack/virtual` remains forbidden: the opt-in `virtual` mode windows the rows itself (spacer padding above and below the rendered slice, sized from a height index: each rendered row is measured with a `ResizeObserver`, rows not yet rendered take the average of the first rows measured (48 px before the first row is measured), and when a row above the rows in view changes height the scroll position moves by the same amount so the rows in view stay still). Without `virtual`, a list of more than 200 rows renders its first 50 rows and mounts the rest as a spacer below them nears the viewport (an `IntersectionObserver`), so a long page costs what is on screen. **Toolbar & imperative API.** The toolbar band composes context-aware controls that drive the table through the injected context with no wiring: `TableFilter` (the slot that hosts `FilterMenu` with `type="menu"`, or `PropertyFilter` with `type="property"`, over its `fields`), `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` with no `fields` in the `filters` slot (the applied fields of the menu type, labelled by the fields the mounted `TableFilter` registers), `CollectionPreferences` with no `columns` (visible columns and their order, written back on Confirm), `TableSearch` (the global text filter, `v-model`), `TableExportButton` (CSV download, `rows` for every match), `TableRefreshButton` and `TableLiveButton` (the live tail, `v-model`). Structured filters are a first-class model (`TableFilter` `v-model`, a `TableAppliedFilter[]` distinct from the free-text search) mapped to the TanStack column filters client-side, or emitted for a server refetch under `manualFiltering`. A `loading` prop renders skeleton rows for dynamic (server-side) data. The root exposes a **curated imperative API** via `defineExpose` (`reload`, `clearFilters`, `exportCsv`, `getSnapshot`, `setSnapshot`) so controls or logic outside the table can drive it through a template ref, and a serializable `TableStateSnapshot` (`sorting` / `page` / `pageSize` / `columnVisibility` / `columnOrder` / `globalFilter` / `filters`) is read with `getSnapshot()` and written back with `setSnapshot()` — the component stays router-agnostic, so the consuming app owns any URL / localStorage persistence. CSV serialization lives in a pure util at [`@aziontech/webkit/utils/csv`](https://github.com/aziontech/webkit/blob/main/packages/webkit/src/utils/csv.ts) (`toCsv` + `downloadCsv`). **Types** (declared in `injection-key.ts`, re-exported for consumers): `TableFilterOperator` = `'eq' | 'neq' | 'contains' | 'not-contains' | 'starts-with' | 'ends-with' | 'gt' | 'gte' | 'lt' | 'lte' | 'in' | 'not-in' | 'is-empty' | 'is-not-empty' | 'within' | 'between'` (`within` holds a period id — `24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `3m` — and matches dates inside that window ending now; `between` holds `[start, end]` epoch milliseconds, either one `''` for an open bound; both read the cell as a `Date`, a timestamp or a parseable date string); `TableFilterType` = `'menu' | 'property'`; `TableFilterField` = `{ id: string; label: string; type: 'text' | 'number' | 'select' | 'multi-select' | 'boolean' | 'date'; operators?: TableFilterOperator[]; options?: { label: string; value: string | number | boolean }[] }`; `TableAppliedFilter` = `{ field: string; operator: TableFilterOperator; value: string | number | boolean | Array<string | number>; label?: string }`; `TableStateSnapshot` = `{ sorting?: SortingState; page?: number; pageSize?: number; columnVisibility?: VisibilityState; columnOrder?: string[]; globalFilter?: string; filters?: TableAppliedFilter[] }` (every field optional so `setSnapshot` accepts a partial; JSON-serializable). **Collections.** `useCollection` (`@aziontech/webkit/use-collection`) drives DataTable in both client and server modes: `tableProps` binds `data` (one page), `columns` (ordered by the saved preferences), `rowKey`, `loading`, `sorting`, `manualSorting` / `manualFiltering`, `selectable`, `selectedKeys`, `columnVisibility` and the three display preferences (`density`, `wrapLines`, `striped`) together with their update handlers, in one `v-bind`; `paginationProps` binds `DataTablePagination` (`v-bind="paginationProps" manual`: `page`, `total`, `pageSize`, `pageSizeOptions` and their handlers). The table keeps rendering one page; the composable owns filtering, sorting, paging and selection across pages, so `exportItems` given to `TableExportButton` `rows` hands the export every match rather than the page: in client mode the matching items (or every item for the `all` scope), in server mode what the collection's `exportAll` callback loads (the loaded page when there is none). **Cell presets and reordering.** The six `TableCell*` presets (each its own import, `@aziontech/webkit/table-cell-<name>`) render the cells every list repeats, each inside a `#cell-<id>` slot: `TableCellLink` (a name that leaves the screen: an optional muted leading glyph (`icon`) for the provider or resource type, a 12 px external mark, a tooltip naming the destination, underline on hover, no mark without a destination; optional `+N` overflow through `OverflowCount` and a copy button pinned to the end edge), `TableCellId` (an identifier with its copy button), `TableCellStatus` (one semantic `Tag`), `TableCellTags` (as many tags as fit, the rest behind `+N`), `TableCellTime` (avatar of the author plus a relative time that updates every minute, or counts from the nearest `ConfigProvider`'s `now`, the absolute time on the tooltip and for screen readers; with no provider `now`, a server render prints the UTC date and the cell switches to the relative time once mounted, so hydration never mismatches) and `TableCellActions` (the row menu named after the row). `reorderable` adds a leading grip column: drag a grip with the pointer, or focus it and press Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home or End; the table emits `update:data` with the reordered records and `reorder` with `{ from, to, row }`, announces every move in a polite status region and locks while a sort is applied; `rowReorderable` keeps chosen rows (a pinned default) in place.
useWhen: Use DataTable for records that share columns — any console list of resources people scan, sort and act on.

Records with the same fields shown in rows and columns, where the reader compares, sorts, selects or acts on rows (resource lists, logs, usage breakdowns): use DataTable for read-and-act lists of repeated records.
A list needs a toolbar for search, structured filters, column visibility, CSV export or refresh — the `Table.*` toolbar parts drive the DataTable through context.
Server-backed data that pages, sorts or filters on the API: `manual-sorting`, `manual-filtering` and a `manual` `DataTablePagination` emit the state instead of slicing locally.
Thousands of rows (`virtual`), tree rows (`get-sub-rows`), reorderable rows, infinite loading or a live tail.
avoidWhen: A small, static table or one whose cells need a layout the column model cannot express → compose it by hand with `table` (no engine in the bundle).
People edit many cells of many records in place, spreadsheet-style → use `data-grid`.
A short list of same-field rows added and removed inside a form (environment variables, headers) → use `attribute-editor`.
A short titled preview of a longer listing on a marketing page → use `listing-table-section`.
A feature-by-feature comparison of Azion with a competitor → use `competitor-comparison-section`.
Rows of mixed content (media, title, description, actions) that do not share columns → use `item`.
The same records as a grid of cards → use `card-list` (same collection, card layout).

In a docs Markdown page or the site's page JSON. DataTable is app-only (decision RV-C2-1, rule `webkit-content-channels`): it drives app state (sorting, selection, paging, filters) through its engine, so it has no `DocMarkdown` tag and no page JSON entry. A docs page writes a Markdown pipe table; the site uses `listing-table-section`.
related: `table` — the parts DataTable renders through, and the hand-composed table for small static content; its toolbar parts and cell presets go in DataTable's slots.
`data-grid` — the editable, spreadsheet-like grid; use it when cells are edited in place.
`pagination` — the page strip; `DataTablePagination` in the `footer` slot renders and wires it.
`listing-table-section` — marketing section that composes `table` for a linked preview of a list.
`empty-state` — the pattern behind the table's default `empty` slot; override the slot for resource-specific copy and actions.
`item` — list rows without a column structure.
`filter-menu` — Use FilterMenu when people filter by picking known values per field (status, region, owner) and see them as chips — the default console list filter; `TableFilter` hosts it by default.

`property-filter` — Use PropertyFilter when people type queries with operators (Status = Active, Requests > 100) or free text they want to keep; `TableFilter type="property"` hosts it wired to the table (AND only).

`collection-preferences` — Use CollectionPreferences for every 'how this list looks' setting: page size, visible and ordered columns, density, wrap; with no `columns` inside the toolbar it edits this table's columns.
bestPractices: For repeated data, pass `data` + `columns` and customize cells with the `cell-<columnId>` / `header-<columnId>` slots instead of composing N rows by hand. Compose `Table` by hand only for small, static tables.
Give rows a stable id under `row-key` (default `'id'`); selection and `v-model:selected-keys` are keyed by it.

When the principal cell repeats another column's value in a phone summary line (a status under the name), set `narrow: false` on that column so a narrow table shows the principal and the actions columns only, never a clipped sliver of the repeated one.
Mark the row-actions column `type: 'action'` so it pins to the trailing edge; give chip or short-token columns a `minWidth` rather than a fixed `width`.

Give `TableCellTime` dates from your data. Where the text must not depend on when it renders (an example, a test, a server render the browser hydrates), set `now` on the app's `ConfigProvider` and count sample dates back from that constant; never build them from `Date.now()` / `new Date()` in setup.
Drive loading through the `loading` prop (skeleton rows, `aria-busy`) and keep the `empty` slot for no-data copy — do not swap the table for a spinner.

On a phone a console list keeps its grid and scrolls sideways (the default). Set `stackable` only for a short list read one record at a time on a narrow, phone-first surface (a marketing listing, a summary in a side panel), where a card per row reads better than a scroll; never on a resource index, a log or a list compared across columns.

Type the rows, not the slot: pass a typed `data` (`ref<Domain[]>([])`, or a literal array) and destructure `#cell-name="{ row, value }"` — `row` is a `Domain` and `value` is `Domain['name']`. Keep a column's `id` equal to its `accessorKey` (or leave `id` out) so the typed `value` is the field the cell shows. Do not annotate the slot scope by hand or cast `row as Domain`; a wrong field (`row.nmae`) should be a type error.

Place `TableSearch`, `TableFilter`, `CollectionPreferences`, `TableExportButton` and `TableRefreshButton` in the `toolbar` slot with no `v-model` wiring — they read the table from context. Import each from its own entry (`@aziontech/webkit/table-search`); they are not attached to the `table` compound.

props.name: maxHeight
props.doc: Max height (CSS length). The viewport scrolls dynamically: horizontal scroll appears automatically when columns overflow the width; vertical scroll appears only when `maxHeight` is set smaller than the content (under the sticky header).

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw the outer card border around the table. Off by default (the table is typically framed by a surrounding surface); set `bordered` / `:bordered="…"` to draw the `var(--border-default)` outline. The internal row dividers are unaffected.

props.name: columns
props.doc: column definitions (`{ id?, accessorKey?, header?, label?, sortable?, grow?, principal?, frozen?, width?, minWidth?, align?, type?, resizable?, hideable?, narrow?, orderable? }`; `width` (px) sets a fixed pixel column (also needed when a frozen column precedes another frozen column on the same edge, so sticky offsets can be summed); **`minWidth`** (px) sets a **floor** instead: the table measures the column's own content — its header, including the sort affordance, and every rendered body cell — and pins the column to the larger of the two, as **one** width applied to the header and every body cell (a per-cell `min-width` would let each row size to its own content and drift the header away from the body). It is for a column whose content is a chip or a short token: a fixed `width` there is a bet in both directions — too generous and it reserves space the rest of the row needs, too tight and the chip inside it truncates. The measured width tracks the **rendered page**, so a column can change width when paging or sorting brings longer content into view; Until the first measurement (and while loading placeholders draw) the column holds its floor, so a loading table on a phone shows the same columns it shows once loaded. `width` wins when both are set, and a user resize wins over both. a `grow` column without `width` keeps a shared fixed basis so the header and body stay aligned and the cell never wraps. A column with no `grow` defaults to weight `2` for the **principal** column and `1` for the rest, so the columns fill the available space proportionally. The principal column is the one flagged `principal: true`, or — when none is flagged — the first non-action column. A `type: 'action'` column is automatically pinned to the trailing (right) edge — staying reachable while the rest scrolls horizontally — and is never resizable. **`resizable: true`** opts a column into a live mouse/touch drag-to-resize handle on its header (native pointer events; the `@tanstack/vue-table` exception covers sorting/pagination/selection/visibility, not sizing). On the first drag of any divider every flexible column freezes at its current rendered width; from then on dragging changes **only that column** and the table grows (horizontal scroll) — the others are untouched. The drag floor is the column's own content width (header label + visible body cells), so a column never shrinks past its content. Frozen and action columns ignore `resizable`. **`label`** names the column in `CollectionPreferences` when `header` is not a string; **`hideable: false`** lists the column locked in `CollectionPreferences`; **`orderable: true`** opts the column into `columnOrder`. **`narrow: false`** drops the column (its header, its cells and its loading placeholders) while the table's own box is narrower than `var(--container-sm)`, for a column whose value the principal cell already repeats there in a phone summary line; the column comes back in a wider box.

props.name: rowKey
props.doc: Field used as the stable row id (for selection).

props.name: sortable
props.doc: Sorts every column on header click; a column's own `sortable` overrides.

props.name: selectable
props.doc: Adds a leading selection-checkbox column.

props.name: rowSelectable
props.doc: decides per row whether it can be selected (`(row) => row.type === 'file'`). A row it rejects draws no checkbox, ignores row clicks and stays out of Select all.

props.name: selectOnRowClick
props.doc: clicking a row toggles its selection (requires `selectable`); interactive cells still own their own click.

props.name: manualSorting
props.doc: Server-side sorting: emit events, do not sort locally.

props.name: manualFiltering
props.doc: Server-side filtering: emit events, do not filter locally.

props.name: loading
props.doc: render skeleton rows in the body (aligned to the visible columns) and set `aria-busy`; `TableRefreshButton` disables/spins while true. Precedence: `loading` → skeleton, else rows, else `empty`.

props.name: error
props.doc: message of a failed load, shown in place of the rows in an `alert` region (an `EmptyState` with the error mark and `table.errorTitle`, the message as its description); the `error` slot replaces it. `loading` wins over it. Empty shows the rows.

props.name: stackable
props.doc: opt in to stacked rows. When the table's own box is narrower than `--container-lg`, each row renders as label and value lines instead of the horizontally scrolling grid. Off by default: a console list scrolls sideways on a phone.

props.name: wrapLines
props.doc: cell text wraps onto several lines instead of truncating.

props.name: striped
props.doc: every other body row takes the raised surface.

props.name: density
props.doc: Density of the header and the body rows: `compact` shrinks their height and padding (the header through `Table.Header`'s `density`). A saved `CollectionPreferences` density therefore covers the whole table.

props.name: virtual
props.doc: render only the rows in view, for thousands of rows. The viewport scrolls vertically within `maxHeight` (40rem when empty). Ignored in the stacked layout.

props.name: reorderable
props.doc: a leading grip column lets people drag rows, or move the focused grip's row with Arrow Up, Arrow Down, Home and End, into a new order. Emits `update:data` (bind `v-model:data`) and `reorder`; locked while a sort is applied.

props.name: rowReorderable
props.doc: With `reorderable`: decides per row whether it can move (`(row) => !row.locked`). A rejected row keeps its place: its grip is disabled, and no row is dropped onto it or moved past it with the keys.

props.name: getSubRows
props.doc: tree rows. Returns a row's children (`(row) => row.children`); a row with children gets an expand toggle in the principal column, its children render under it indented one step (`--spacing-md`) per level, and the grid element takes `role="treegrid"`. Sorting and filtering keep each child under its parent; selection is per row (selecting a parent does not select its children). `reorderable` is ignored in tree mode.

props.name: data
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:data`).

props.name: sorting
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:sorting`).

props.name: selectedKeys
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:selectedKeys`).

props.name: columnVisibility
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:columnVisibility`).

props.name: openKeys
props.doc: Two-way value (`v-model:openKeys`).

events.name: row-click
events.notes: Fires when a rendered row is clicked, or when `Enter` is pressed on a focused row (keyboard rows, below). `event` is the click or the key press; `row` is the record.

events.name: row-remove
events.notes: `Delete` (or `Backspace`, which a Mac keyboard's delete key sends) was pressed on a focused row. The table removes nothing: the app asks first (a `ConfirmDialog`) and then drops the record from `data`.

events.name: filter-apply
events.notes: `TableFilter` committed a pick or a token — the explicit re-query signal for `manualFiltering`.

events.name: filter-remove
events.notes: One applied filter was removed (a `FilterMenu.ChipGroup` chip).

events.name: refresh
events.notes: Refresh requested; the app refetches. `event` is the click of `TableRefreshButton`, or `new Event('refresh')` when `reload()` is called.

events.name: export
events.notes: Export requested with the resolved rows; `event` is the click of `TableExportButton`, or `new Event('export')` when `exportCsv()` is called; a consumer may handle it server-side (otherwise the built-in CSV util downloads).

events.name: reorder
events.payload: (event: KeyboardEvent | PointerEvent, payload: { from: number; to: number; row: TRow })
events.notes: `reorderable`: a row moved from index `from` to index `to` of `data`.

slots.name: caption
slots.notes: caption content (wrapped in TableCaption), fixed above the scroll viewport.

slots.name: title
slots.notes: Title text shown at the start of the toolbar band, fixed above the scroll viewport.

slots.name: toolbar
slots.notes: Action band (search, filter, refresh, export, column preferences) above the scroll viewport, end-aligned beside the title. `table` is the TanStack instance; `selectedRows` / `selectedCount` / `clearSelection` expose the selection for bulk-action toolbars, and `loading` mirrors the prop.

slots.name: filters
slots.notes: Active-filter chips row below the toolbar; same scope as `toolbar`.

slots.name: empty
slots.notes: shown when there are no rows. Defaults to an empty-state block (illustration + title + description) following Figma; override the slot for custom copy/actions.

slots.name: error
slots.notes: shown in place of the rows while `error` is set; `message` is the `error` prop. Defaults to a small `EmptyState` with the error mark, `table.errorTitle` and the message.

slots.name: load-more
slots.notes: content after the last row that scrolls with the rows, inside the viewport: `DataTableLoadMore`.

slots.name: footer
slots.notes: band below the scroll viewport, outside `role="table"`: `DataTablePagination`.
